about: Plants regulated by law, as each rule names them: docs/regulated-plants.md. Each class's tier: ban (the rule forbids selling, planting or moving it) or listed (it lists the plant, with lighter duties). Matched to the catalog by Kew's accepted names (scripts/catalog/regulated.mjs).

jurisdictions.title: Federal noxious weeds (7 CFR 360.200)
jurisdictions.edition: Code of Federal Regulations, revised as of January 1, 2025; §360.200 last amended 2010 (75 FR 68953)

classes.noxious: Federal noxious weed: bringing it into or through the United States, or moving it from state to state, needs a USDA permit (7 CFR 360.300)

jurisdictions.notes: Genus entries take in every species, variety and form in the genus but those the rule excepts (its footnote); the exceptions are matched by their printed names. Left out: Caulerpa taxifolia, an alga. Avena ludoviciana is in "Avena sterilis (including Avena ludoviciana)"; Kew makes it a subspecies, so it is matched by its printed name. Missiongrass (Pennisetum polystachion): Kew types the name on a native grass, Setaria parviflora, so it is matched by its printed names only. Rubus fruticosus "(complex)": matched as the one species; its segregates (R. armeniacus) are not.

jurisdictions.title: Arkansas Plant Board rules (2 CAR §50-101, §50-709)

classes.prohibited: Prohibited in Arkansas: no plant, seed or any reproductive structure of it may be sold or planted (2 CAR §50-101(f))
classes.lythrum: Prohibited in Arkansas: no Lythrum may be planted, sold, bought or moved (2 CAR §50-709)
classes.noxious: Declared a noxious weed and public nuisance in Arkansas: nursery stock must be reasonably free of it (2 CAR §50-101; §50-302)

jurisdictions.notes: Every species §50-101(d) and (f) name, and every genus it lists whole: dodder (Cuscuta spp.), Rumex spp., witchweed (Striga spp.), Crotalaria spp., cocklebur (Xanthium spp.), and the thistle genera it names (Carduus, Cirsium, Onopordum, Silybum, Scolymus, Salsola), natives in them too: the rule takes them in. Lythrum is the whole genus and its hybrids by §50-709 (purple loosestrife is on (d) and (f) too: shown by §50-709, which says more). Read narrower than printed, where a common name says which plants are meant: "wild onion and/or wild garlic (Allium spp.)" as wild onion, Allium canadense, and wild garlic, Allium vineale; "alligatorweed (Alternanthera spp.)" as alligatorweed, A. philoxeroides. Left out: "morning glory (Ipomoea spp.)", which names no species, and read whole would make the sweet potato a noxious weed; the thistle entry's "and other genera", which names none; red rice, "Oryza sativa var.", which names no variety (the species is rice).

jurisdictions.title: Texas noxious and invasive plant list (4 TAC §19.300; Agriculture Code §71.152)
jurisdictions.edition: Figure: 4 TAC §19.300(a), as published by the Texas Department of Agriculture; Agriculture Code §71.152 as amended 2005 (Texas Legislature)

classes.noxious: Noxious plant in Texas: selling it, distributing it or bringing it into the state, in any live form, is a misdemeanor, unless permitted (Texas Agriculture Code §71.152; 4 TAC §19.300)
classes.invasive: On Texas's invasive plant list: selling it, distributing it or bringing it into the state, in any live form, is a misdemeanor, unless permitted (Texas Agriculture Code §71.152; 4 TAC §19.300)

jurisdictions.notes: Chinese tallow, kudzu, saltcedar and tropical soda apple are on both lists: shown as noxious. The offense is the statute's (§71.152: a Class C misdemeanor, each item sold, distributed or imported a separate offense); "in any live form" and "unless permitted" are the rule's, §19.300(b), read through Cornell LII's copy of the rule until the Secretary of State's can be read.

jurisdictions.title: Louisiana: Chinese tallow (La. R.S. 3:1791)

classes.noxious: Recognized as a noxious plant in Louisiana: it may be destroyed wherever found (La. R.S. 3:1791)

jurisdictions.notes: Louisiana's noxious weed list (LAC 7:XIII.109) limits weed seed in seed for sale; it says nothing of live plants, and is left out.

jurisdictions.title: Tennessee pest plant regulations (Tenn. Comp. R. & Regs. 0080-06-24)
jurisdictions.edition: Rules of the Tennessee Department of Agriculture, chapter 0080-06-24, revised April 2009 (effective 2009-04-13)

classes.pest: Pest plant in Tennessee: it may not be sold, offered for sale or released in the state, nor propagated without a permit from the commissioner (Tenn. Comp. R. & Regs. 0080-06-24)

jurisdictions.notes: Rule .02 lists 13 entries; Lythrum salicaria and L. virgatum share one ("and related cultivars"), so 14 names. The phase-in dates for privets, bush honeysuckles, multiflora rose and the olives (retail 2010 to 2012, wholesale 2012 to 2014) have all passed. Rule .03 allows propagating, collecting and selling under a permit (a compliance agreement, for research and propagative purposes), so long as the plants are kept from sale or release in Tennessee; it never allows selling them within Tennessee. The PDF was saved by hand: the Secretary of State's file host turns away clients that aren't browsers.
